definitions.explanation: A samurai who has lost or left his lord and so has no fixed stipend. A historical word, met mostly in accounts of the Edo period and the Bakumatsu years.

examples.japanese: {浪士|ろうし}たち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まった→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
{赤穂|あこう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{浪士|ろうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{主君|しゅくん}→主君：11712_shukun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{仇|かたき}→仇：11476_kataki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{討|う}った→討つ：14820_utsu⟧。
examples.english: The masterless samurai of Akō avenged their lord.

examples.japanese: ⟦{幕末|ばくまつ}→幕末：12531_bakumatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{全国|ぜんこく}→全国：03311_zenkoku⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{浪士|ろうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{集|あつ}まっていた→集まる：01162_atsumaru⟧。
examples.english: In Kyoto at the end of the shogunate, many masterless samurai had gathered from all over the country.

notes:
A historical word for a samurai without a master. It appears mainly in the names of famous groups and in history writing.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {赤穂浪士|あこうろうし}: the forty-seven ronin of Akō, the heroes of ⟦{忠臣蔵|ちゅうしんぐら}→忠臣蔵：31064_chuushingura⟧
- {浪士組|ろうしぐみ}: the band of ronin that became the {新選組|しんせんぐみ}
- {脱藩|だっぱん}{浪士|ろうし}: a ronin who had fled his domain

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{浪人|ろうにん}→浪人：13301_rounin⟧: the everyday word for the same thing; today it also means a student who failed the entrance exams and is preparing to retake them. {浪士|ろうし} has no modern sense and sounds more dignified.
